overview.description: YouTube is a video website, owned by Google, where anyone can upload, watch, and make money from videos — everything from short clips (Shorts) to long videos, music, and live TV/sports — available in over 100 countries and 80 languages.
overview.vision: To give everyone a voice and show them the world.
problemsSolved: Lets anyone publish video content to a global audience without needing a TV network or cable deal
Gives advertisers a huge, targeted pool of video viewers to show ads to
Gives creators ways to earn money from their videos (a share of ad revenue, channel memberships, etc.), so they can turn making videos into a business
Offers people who've cancelled cable TV a live-TV and sports bundle (YouTube TV, NFL Sunday Ticket) as an alternative

stats.revenue: $11.06 billion in ad money made in just the second quarter (Apr-Jun) of 2026 (up 12.6% from a year earlier, per Alphabet's earnings report); YouTube's full financials aren't reported separately from the rest of Google

businessModel.summary: Mostly makes money from ads, with a smaller subscription business on top whose exact size isn't made public.

items.detail: Ads shown across regular videos, Shorts, and on TV screens — this brought in $11.06 billion in just three months (Q2 2026), up 12.6% from a year earlier.
Paid plans like YouTube Premium (no ads + music), YouTube Music, YouTube TV, and NFL Sunday Ticket — Google doesn't publish how much money these bring in separately.

items.name: Chad Hurley
items.background: Used to design products at PayPal, including its original logo. Led YouTube as CEO through its early growth and its sale to Google.

items.name: Steve Chen
items.background: One of PayPal's first employees. Handled much of YouTube's early technical build-out.

items.name: Jawed Karim
items.background: A software engineer at PayPal. He uploaded YouTube's very first video, an 18-second clip called 'Me at the zoo,' then left fairly early on to go get a master's degree at Stanford.

items.event: Steve Chen, Chad Hurley, and Jawed Karim register the YouTube.com website address (Feb 14) and start the company, working out of Chad Hurley's garage; investment firm Sequoia Capital provides the first funding.
YouTube officially opens to the public (Dec 15), and is already getting more than 2 million video views a day.
Google buys YouTube for $1.65 billion, paid entirely in Google stock rather than cash (announced Oct 9, deal completed Nov 13) — at the time, Google's biggest purchase ever.
YouTube says it has passed 2 billion people logging in every month, up from 1.9 billion a year earlier.
Launches YouTube Shorts (short video clips) — first in India (Sept 2020), then the US (Mar 2021) — as a direct response to TikTok's rise.

Wins the rights to stream NFL 'Sunday Ticket' games in a 7-year deal reportedly worth roughly $2 billion a year (about $14 billion total), taking that package over from satellite-TV provider DirecTV starting the 2023 season.
Neal Mohan takes over as YouTube's CEO from Susan Wojcicki (Feb 16), who had led the company for 9 years and stays on to advise Google/Alphabet leadership.

NFL Sunday Ticket runs into trouble twice: a mobile-app outage during a live game week (Sept), and a separate dispute with Disney/ESPN that temporarily locked some paying subscribers out of channels they'd already paid for (Oct-Nov).

Tightens and clarifies its rules on what AI-generated videos can and can't earn ad money from (Jul), after already removing channels that together had over 35 million subscribers and roughly $10M a year in ad earnings.

sources.label: Google Inc. official filing with financial regulators

items: Ask YouTube (AI feature that answers questions about videos)

items.challenge: Balancing AI-made videos against creator trust and platform quality
items.details: In July 2026, YouTube spelled out clearer rules on what kind of content can't earn ad money — mass-produced/formulaic AI videos, emotionally manipulative content, and AI-generated 'people' discussing sensitive topics like health or finance. The rules have real teeth: 16 channels with a combined 4.7 billion views and about $10 million a year in ad earnings lost their ability to earn money in a single wave. But critics say the system still lets clever bad actors slip through while sometimes wrongly punishing genuine creators.

items.challenge: Reliability and trust problems with its premium NFL Sunday Ticket product
items.details: Since winning the rights to NFL Sunday Ticket, YouTube has had a mobile-app outage during a live game (Sept 2025) and a separate dispute with Disney/ESPN that temporarily locked some paying customers out of channels they'd already paid for (Oct-Nov 2025) — with no way to cancel without losing the Sunday Ticket package too. Both incidents drew criticism given the high price (up to about $480 for the season).

items.text: The interview process usually includes a recruiter call, a coding interview (often solving a problem in a shared document), and conversations about team fit. Both Glassdoor and Blind reviews describe YouTube's engineering culture as better than the average at Google for work-life balance and having leaders who are held accountable, with people mentioning hackathons and getting to actually ship features that matter — though some say the team can feel a bit cut off from Google's bigger Search/Ads business.

Reviewers describe a long interview process with little feedback afterward, including questions about how to handle tricky situations with content creators or business partners. This is based on Glassdoor reviews only and hasn't been checked against a second source.

Reviews describe a multi-step hiring process that includes a take-home writing/analysis assignment, with some candidates saying they got slow or unclear responses afterward. Given YouTube's active push against AI-generated content, expect interview questions that test your judgment on gray-area content decisions. This is based on Glassdoor reviews only and hasn't been checked against a second source.
